title: COSTA: Covariance-Preserving Feature Augmentation for Graph Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Graph contrastive learning depends on graph augmentation, and the resulting node embeddings can be highly biased, limiting the learning of discriminative downstream features.

gap.claim: The graph augmentation step in graph contrastive learning is vital but scarcely studied, particularly beyond augmentations in the input space.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes feature augmentation in the hidden feature space instead of investigating augmentation in the input space.
COSTA is a covariance-preserving feature-space augmentation framework for graph contrastive learning that generates augmented features by maintaining a good sketch of the original features.
The paper investigates a single-view setting alongside a multi-view setting to conserve memory and computation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe COSTA as a novel covariance-preserving feature-space augmentation framework for graph contrastive learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that feature augmentation with COSTA achieves comparable or better results than graph-augmentation-based models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph contrastive learning improves graph representation learning and has achieved state-of-the-art results on various downstream tasks.
Graph augmentation is vital to graph contrastive learning but has been scarcely studied.
Graph augmentations produce highly biased node embeddings, motivating augmentation in the hidden feature space.
COSTA performs covariance-preserving feature-space augmentation by maintaining a good sketch of the original features.
The paper considers single-view and multi-view settings and reports comparable or better results than graph-augmentation-based models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract attributes biased node embeddings to graph augmentation and proposes augmenting hidden features instead.

interpretation.claim: When input-space transformations introduce undesirable representation bias, augmentation at a learned intermediate representation may be a useful alternative.

application.claim: For graph contrastive learning systems, compare input-space graph augmentation with feature-space augmentation when designing representations for downstream tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when feature augmentation is preferable across datasets, tasks, or augmentation regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the matrix-sketching procedure or the meaning of a good sketch in operational detail.
The abstract does not report computational or memory measurements for the single-view setting.
